**3B.2 Research Note**

Mixed, with stronger evidence on the negative side. Srettha’s government made some formal rights-protective gestures in 2024, but the same year still saw arbitrary detention, a custodial death, and continued impunity for past security-force abuse. I found no strong evidence that he systematically punished abusive police or military actors.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Thailand ratifies disappearance convention, urges law on torture and enforced disappearance | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-05-16 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/icpped140524-2?page=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aaf9 | Thailand deposited ratification of the disappearance treaty and said its anti-torture / anti-disappearance law would be an important tool. This is the clearest formal step toward preventing abuses by state organs. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Positive | Prime Minister delivers statement at 3rd Summit for Democracy, highlighting Thailand’s commitment to democracy, rule of law, and human rights at home and abroad | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-03-20 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-3-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Srettha publicly aligned his government with democracy, rule of law, and human rights. This is supportive intent evidence, but it is not proof that abusive security actors were actually disciplined. | 3B.2 |
| Positive | Thai Prime Minister Promises Investigation After Activist Died in Detention | Khaosod English / Associated Press | 2024-05-15 | https://www.khaosodenglish.com/politics/2024/05/15/thai-prime-minister-promises-investigation-after-activist-died-in-detention/ | After activist Netiporn Sanesangkhom died in custody, Srettha promised an investigation. That is limited accountability evidence, though it stops short of showing punishment or structural reform. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Negative | Thailand: Tragic death of detained activist must be ‘wake-up call’ | Amnesty International | 2024-05-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/thailand-tragic-death-of-detained-activist-must-be-wake-up-call/ | Amnesty said Netiporn had been held in arbitrary detention for peaceful protest and died in custody. That is direct evidence of tolerated abuse inside the detention system, absent a prompt effective response. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Negative | Thailand: Investigate Detained Youth Activist’s Death | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-23 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/23/thailand-investigate-detained-youth-activists-death | HRW said hundreds of monarchy critics were in pretrial detention and urged an end to arbitrary detention and prosecution. This indicates continued tolerance of coercive abuse by the justice/security apparatus. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Negative | Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-01 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice | HRW said successive Thai governments had failed to prosecute those responsible for the Tak Bai crackdown deaths and injuries. That is strong evidence of long-running impunity for security-force violence that Srettha did not resolve in 2024. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |

**Assessment**
- Best-supported reading: Srettha showed limited preventive/accountability steps, but not enough to show a real crackdown on abusive police, prison, or military conduct.
- Strongest negative evidence: arbitrary detention of peaceful protesters, a death in custody, and unresolved impunity for prior mass-casualty security-force abuses.
- Search gap: I did not find a 2024 source showing Srettha directly ordering punishment of abusive officers, dismantling abusive units, or credibly ending institutional tolerance for torture/arbitrary detention.
